_comment: Attribution of the mask/engine refusals counted in contract_channels_20260919.json, by the phase
the decision was made in, plus what the filter-mode re-ask then executed. Measured with
scripts/census_rejection_phases.py over three disjoint 500-seed shards of the act1 promotion
partition (same checkpoint every census figure in the report uses), keyed to the state BEFORE the
step so a refusal is matched to the decision it refused.
Why this was worth measuring: illegal_actions cannot be non-zero in filter mode, so the phase
distribution is what tells a reader which campaign numbers the refusals can touch.
The per-shard rows below are the raw output of the three runs, minus the checkpoint path, the
per-shard digest (identical across the three, so recorded once above) and the timestamp; two
launch fields, start_offset and limit, were added to identify each window. The aggregation is
their exact elementwise sum, and verify_report_claims.py recomputes it from these rows rather
decisions_total, reward_screen_decisions and the two per-phase rates are derived from the shard rows, not hand-added; the report quotes these fields.
established: every refusal in 1,500 episodes lands in exactly two phases: shop (641 of 2,866 shop decisions) and event (112 of 4,305)

combat is clean: 0 refusals across 130,993 combat decisions, and so are the two reward screens that the boss-exit fork conclusions rest on: 0 of 17,698 relic_reward and 0 of 5,459 card_reward decisions
when the engine refuses an advertised action the re-ask always executes something different: 503 of 503 refusal states ended in an action the policy had not chosen first

the per-episode refusal rate measured this way (0.502) is the same order as the independently computed campaign counter for this stage/split (0.530 per the contract-channels census), so the two paths agree rather than one being derived from the other
not_established: why the shop and event masks advertise actions their own step refuses -- affordability and event-option limits are plausible and testable (compare the refused base against the shop cost vector at that state), but nothing was measured here
that shop/event behaviour is identical on other checkpoints; this is one checkpoint, though it is the one every census figure in the report uses
how much the shop refusals shift deck strength, and therefore how much of the act-1 deficit is entangled with them
anything about potion_reward: the phase never occurs in these 1,500 episodes, so it is unobserved here, not measured clean -- 'reward screens are clean' covers relic_reward and card_reward only
scope: simulator_act1 label, mixed-act population, argmax, one checkpoint, 1,500 seeds
verdict: the refusals that filter mode hides from illegal_actions are a shop/event phenomenon; every number in this report about combat behaviour and about boss reward-screen action choice is measured on states where no refusal occurred
